assumptions.ruleset: Gathering Storm with every expansion and the Leader Pass
assumptions.map: Pangaea or Continents, standard size, 8 civilizations
assumptions.notes: Turn numbers are Standard-speed scaffolding; the site rescales them for other speeds and difficulties. This plans Saladin (Vizier), the base-game persona named in the leader record, not the Leader Pass Saladin (Sultan).

verdict.one_line: Skip the Faith race, put the Production it would have cost into Settlers and Campuses, have one Holy Site ready when the last Prophet arrives, and choose by turn 80 whether the Madrasa Faith converts neighbours for Science, converts them for the win, or buys Mamluks.
verdict.why: The Last Prophet removes the race every other religious civilization has to run, so the Production that would have gone into Shrines, Holy Sites and Temples before turn 60 goes into Settlers and Campuses, and the religion still arrives. That is tempo, not a win, and it disappears if it is banked. Science is the default because the Madrasa turns Campus adjacency into both Science and Faith, the Faith buys the Worship building for a tenth of its price and the Missionaries that make every converted foreign city pay +1 Science, and none of it expires. Religion is second rather than Domination because the same Faith that converts neighbours for Science can convert them for the win when the late religion still has room, while the Mamluk window is one era long.

must_have: Mountains, Geothermal Fissures or Reefs beside at least half the city sites, because the Madrasa's Faith equals the Campus adjacency and the plan has almost no other Faith.
At least two neighbours reachable by land or a short sea crossing, since The Last Prophet pays Science only for foreign cities that follow the religion.
prefer: Desert or Desert Hills around the capital, for Petra, for Desert Folklore if Divine Spark is gone, and for the one Holy Site's adjacency.
Dead Sea, Delicate Arch or Sahara el Beyda in reach; Faith or Gold on tiles that otherwise yield nothing.
Floodplains or a river through the desert, so the Campus cities grow to staff their Madrasas.
map_check.no_go: A small island alone, or a start where every neighbour already follows one strong religion by turn 80 with Apostles on the border. The late religion converts nobody, The Last Prophet's Science is zero, and Arabia becomes an ordinary Science civilization with a better University.
map_check.fallback: Play the Science direction without the religious half: found the religion anyway for the Worship building at a tenth of its cost and the +10% Science, Faith and Culture in every Arabian city that has it, hold the home cities with the Holy City's pressure, and spend the Madrasa Faith on Great Scientists instead of Missionaries.

kit_levers.name: Righteousness of the Faith
kit_levers.buys: The Worship building Arabia's religion picks can be bought by any civilization for a tenth of the normal Faith, and Arabian cities that have it get +10% Science, Faith and Culture.
kit_levers.exploit: Evangelize the Worship belief with the first Apostle, then buy the building in every Arabian city with a Temple the turn the Temple finishes. At a tenth of the cost it is the cheapest percentage bonus in the game, and taking the Wat when it is still free stacks its flat Science on top of the percentage.

kit_levers.name: The Last Prophet
kit_levers.buys: Arabia receives the final Great Prophet automatically when the next-to-last one is claimed, if it has not earned one already, and +1 Science for every foreign city following its religion.
kit_levers.exploit: Build no Shrine, Holy Site or Temple for the race; build one Holy Site to receive the Prophet and put everything else into Settlers and Campuses. After founding, every Missionary that converts a foreign city is permanent Science, so the Faith is aimed at neighbours' cities once home is safe.

kit_levers.name: Mamluk
kit_levers.buys: A Knight replacement with the Knight's Combat Strength that heals at the end of every turn, even after moving or attacking.
kit_levers.exploit: The Domination direction: five Mamluks and two Trebuchets never stop to heal, and with Crusade evangelized they fight at +10 beside cities the Missionaries have already converted. On the other directions two Mamluks clear the late camps and hold the border.

kit_levers.name: Madrasa
kit_levers.buys: A University replacement with more Science than the University and Faith equal to the Campus district's adjacency bonus.
kit_levers.exploit: The plan's Faith engine. Campuses go beside Mountains, Geothermal Fissures and other districts from turn 20 so that each Madrasa later pays three or four Faith a turn as well as Science; that Faith buys the Worship buildings, the Missionaries and, under Theocracy on the Domination direction, the Mamluks.

kit_levers.name: Ayyubid Dynasty
kit_levers.buys: Saladin likes civilizations that have his religion's Worship building and dislikes those that follow another religion or fight his faith's followers.
kit_levers.exploit: Only matters for AI Saladin: an AI Arabia pushes its religion late into everyone's cities, so a religious civilization should treat him as the theological rival rather than a friend.

options.when_it_fits: Five or more Campuses with +2 or better adjacency by turn 80 and two neighbours with eight or more cities between them inside Missionary reach. Madrasas turn adjacency into Science and Faith, the Faith buys Worship buildings and Missionaries, and every converted foreign city is permanent Science; nothing in the kit expires on this path.

The religion is founded by turn 85, the Mosque or another spread belief is still free, and no rival religion is the majority in more than two civilizations. Madrasa Faith and Theocracy buy Apostles faster than most religious AIs and Jerusalem makes every Holy Site push like a Holy City; take it only when the map has left room, because a late founder starts every theological fight behind.

A neighbour within ten tiles has no Walls beyond Ancient ones at turn 80, and Missionaries can convert two of its cities before Stirrups. Crusade gives +10 Combat Strength near converted foreign cities, Mamluks heal every turn so the siege never pauses, and Theocracy lets the Madrasa Faith buy them; the window closes when the target fields Musketmen.

direction.commit_test: At turn 120 read the religion and the queues. Science has the Worship building in every Temple city, Madrasas in three cities and Missionaries walking to foreign cities; Religion has Theocracy, two Apostles out and the Holy City buying more; Domination has Crusade evangelized, five Mamluks and two Trebuchets at the border. A little of each, or Faith piling up unspent, is the banked bonus and the plan has failed its own test.

phases.name: Campuses, not Shrines
phases.objective: Put the Production other civilizations spend on Shrines and Holy Sites into Settlers and Campuses: four cities and two Campuses beside Mountains by turn 45, a pantheon bought with God King's Faith alone, and a Scout's count of who is building Holy Sites, because the turn the next-to-last Great Prophet is claimed is the turn Arabia's Prophet arrives.

Archery Eureka on a camp scout, and the only defender the capital needs while Settlers leave.
Second city by turn 15 toward the nearest Mountains; no Shrine is ever queued ahead of a Settler.
A Farm on Wheat or a Floodplains resource for Irrigation, a Mine on a resource for The Wheel, a third improvement for Craftsmanship.
Capital Campus beside a Mountain the turn Writing lands; State Workforce Inspiration, and the Madrasa's Faith later equals this adjacency.
Third city once Colonization is slotted from Early Empire.
Divine Spark pays only on a Campus with a Library, and the Madrasa needs it.
Fourth city; this is the Settler a rival spent on its Shrine and Temple.

Six population across two cities; Colonization for Settlers three and four.
The capital Campus gives the Inspiration; Political Philosophy is behind it.
Founding the pantheon gives the Inspiration; the Inspiration policy card for Great Scientist points comes from it.

policies.why: The only Faith Arabia makes before turn 40; the pantheon lands near turn 30 on it.
The Slinger and Warrior clear the camps that threaten the Settlers.
Replaces God King the turn after the pantheon; +50% Production toward Settlers, kept until city seven.

districts.note: Beside one or more Mountains, a Geothermal Fissure or a Reef; leave room beside it for the next districts, since a +3 Campus is a three-Faith Madrasa later.

pantheon.why: A Great Scientist point from every Campus with a Library, which is what this opening builds instead of Holy Sites, and the first Great Scientist is the Education Eureka.

city_states.why: The first envoys go to a Scientific city-state: Science in the capital now and in every Library at three envoys.
If met, suzerainty is +15% Science in every city while at peace, which is the Science direction's normal state.

checkpoints.test: Two cities, the capital Campus placed beside a Mountain, God King slotted and no Shrine or Holy Site built anywhere?
checkpoints.pass: Keep the Settler chain going; the pantheon lands within five turns.
checkpoints.fail: A Shrine or Holy Site in a queue is the Faith race this kit was excused from; cancel it and put a Settler there. No second city by turn 25 means the Builder went ahead of the Settler; swap them for city three.

checkpoints.test: Four cities, two Campuses with a Library in the capital, the pantheon founded, and a note of which rivals have Holy Sites and how many religions exist?
checkpoints.pass: Enter the waiting phase; the Holy Site that will receive the Prophet is the next district after Campus three.
checkpoints.fail: Three cities is acceptable with the fourth Settler walking. No pantheon by turn 45 means God King came off too early; put it back until the 25 Faith are in. No count of rival Holy Sites means the Prophet's date is a guess; send the Scout or a Warrior to the unmet rivals.

tasks.text: Settle on the spot or one move toward a Mountain or a river; the capital Campus wants two Mountains beside it.
Scout toward the nearest rivals and note every Holy Site seen; three rival Holy Sites by turn 30 mean the last Prophet comes early.
Capital Campus started on the best Mountain tile; State Workforce Inspiration on completion.
Found Divine Spark with God King's Faith, or Desert Folklore if the capital is ringed by Desert; then swap God King for Colonization.
Fourth city founded; every city's first district is a Campus, never a Holy Site.

phases.name: Waiting for the last Prophet
phases.objective: Reach seven cities with a Campus in each and Libraries in the best three, finish one Holy Site in the best Desert or Mountain city before the third rival religion is founded, decide the direction by turn 80 from what the belief lists and the neighbours offer, and found the religion the turn the last Prophet arrives.

First district in every new city, Mountain or district adjacency first.
One, in the city with the most Desert or a Mountain beside it, finished before the next-to-last religion is founded so the Prophet can found on arrival.
Missionaries need it, and the Holy Site's adjacency makes it the empire's only Faith until the Madrasas.
In the three best Campuses; Divine Spark and the Inspiration card push the first Great Scientist.
Currency Eureka; a domestic route into the capital carries Food and Production.
The third district type for the Mathematics Eureka, and Gold to buy Settlers.
In the Holy Site city right after founding; Apostles and the Worship building both need it.

Adopt Classical Republic the turn Political Philosophy lands; Natural Philosophy in an Economic slot and Inspiration in the Wildcard slot.
Write the direction down: Science, Religion or Domination, with the neighbour and the beliefs that decided it.
Found the religion in the Holy Site the turn the Prophet appears, taking the shortlist's first free Founder and Follower beliefs; queue the Temple.

decision_triggers.name: Religions come early
decision_triggers.if: Three religions are founded before turn 50.
decision_triggers.then: The last Prophet is one founding away. Finish the Holy Site now, ahead of the next Campus, and have the belief shortlist written by turn 55; pick the direction early from what is left.

decision_triggers.name: Prophet runs late
decision_triggers.if: Turn 75 with two or fewer religions founded.
decision_triggers.then: The Prophet may not come until the Medieval era. Do not race for it; the Science direction needs no religion before the Madrasas. Keep the Holy Site, add a Shrine so Missionaries can be bought the turn the religion exists, and if Religion was the leaning, switch to Science.

decision_triggers.name: Jesuit Education is left
decision_triggers.if: Jesuit Education is still free when the Prophet founds.
decision_triggers.then: Take it as the Follower belief whatever the direction: Madrasa Faith then buys Libraries and Madrasas directly, which is worth more to this kit than any other Follower belief.

decision_triggers.name: Heresy at home
decision_triggers.if: An Arabian city's majority religion is foreign, or rival Apostles are within three tiles of a Madrasa city.
decision_triggers.then: Buy a Missionary in the Holy City and convert the city back that turn, with Moksha as Bishop holding the pressure. On the Religion direction launch an Inquisition with an Apostle instead and remove the heresy with Inquisitors.

decision_triggers.name: Converted neighbour in reach
decision_triggers.if: By turn 110 two cities of a neighbour within ten tiles follow the religion and it has no Medieval Walls.
decision_triggers.then: On the Domination direction evangelize Crusade with the second Apostle and march the Mamluks with Trebuchets. On Science leave the neighbour alone; its converted cities pay Science every turn it lives.

abort.trigger: Turn 150 with no direction committed: Faith banked above the price of three Missionaries, the Worship building in fewer than half the Temple cities, no foreign city converted and no capital taken.
actions: Commit to Science, which a Madrasa empire is always closest to; Linear leaders lose by drifting, not by collapsing.
Spend the banked Faith today: the Worship building in every Temple city, then Missionaries into the nearest foreign cities, or Great Scientists with Faith if none is in reach.
Reroute the civic queue toward The Enlightenment, Class Struggle and Space Race, and put a Madrasa in every Campus city before any other building.

fail_state: Turn 200 with eight cities, a Campus in each and a religion founded on time, Faith piling up unspent, the Worship building in two cities, no foreign city following the religion and a Science rate that is merely good. Arabia skipped the Faith race and spent the saving on nothing in particular; the Prophet came, the religion sits in its own cities, and The Last Prophet's Science bonus has never paid once.
common_mistakes: Building a Shrine or Holy Site in the first thirty turns to race for a Prophet that is already guaranteed. That Production is the whole advantage.
Having no Holy Site when the Prophet arrives. It can found only in one, and every turn it waits a rival can take the belief on the shortlist.
Founding with first-choice beliefs in mind. The Prophet is last; read what is left, rank it before turn 70, and pick from the list.
Converting Arabia's own cities and calling it spreading. The Last Prophet pays only for foreign cities; Missionaries go to neighbours once home is safe.
Banking Madrasa Faith. At a tenth of the price the Worship buildings cost almost nothing; the rest is Missionaries, Apostles or Great Scientists, every turn.
sources: Civilization VI Civilopedia, Gathering Storm ruleset (Arabia, Saladin, Mamluk, Madrasa, religion and beliefs).

The civ-info text gives the Worship building's bonus to every city that has it; in the game the +10% Science, Faith and Culture applies to Arabian cities only, and other civilizations get the purchase discount but not the bonus. The plan follows the game.
